text:
CHIEF FINDING, and I initially recorded this as an OPEN DESIGN QUESTION in docs/design/adr-0003-migration-status.md; checking the wiring made it decidable and it is a defect. TWO PARTS.

PART 1 - THE WIRING. NodeSummary.importance defaults to Estimate.observed(1.0). The ONLY production construction site is StorySourceView.summarize (bridge/StorySourceView.scala:98), which passes positional arguments through 'lemmas' and then jumps to 'evidence = ...' BY NAME - it never passes importance. So every node produced by the only production bridge carries observed(1.0). Nothing else in */src/main/scala sets it; the sole other writer is laws/AlignGens.scala, a generator.

PART 2 - THE ARITHMETIC, verified by hand against signature.scala:91-96. uniform = leaves.map(visitation).sum / leaves.size. weighted = importance.map((r,w) => w*visitation(r)).sum / wsum. With every w = 1.0, wsum = leaves.size and weighted reduces to sum(visitation)/leaves.size, which is EXACTLY uniform. So RecallSignature publishes uniformCoverage and importanceWeightedCoverage as two fields that are IDENTICAL BY CONSTRUCTION in every real run.

WHY P1: this is not redundancy, it is a scientific claim. A researcher comparing the two numbers finds them always equal and may conclude that importance weighting does not affect coverage for these recalls - a finding about the data caused entirely by a wiring gap in our pipeline. That is the estimand disease in a new key: an unavailable INPUT silently rendered as a uniform prior, and the resulting number published under a name asserting it measured something else.

PART 2b - A SEPARATE DEFECT IN THE CODE ITSELF, independent of the wiring: 'if wsum <= 0 then uniform'. When every importance is Missing, the weighted figure is filled in with the UNIFORM figure - a different measurement published under the weighted name. The adjacent comment shows the right instinct ('Leaves whose importance is Missing are excluded from the weighted sum (never counted as 0)') and then the all-Missing case substitutes rather than abstaining. Correct behaviour is Missing with a reason: we were given no importances, so importance-weighted coverage is not computable.

FIX DIRECTION: (a) all-Missing must yield Missing, never uniform; (b) decide and document whether the observed(1.0) default is legitimate - a uniform prior is a defensible modelling choice, but if it is kept it must be DECLARED so that the two fields' equality is expected rather than discovered, and the default should arguably be Missing so that a caller who supplies no importances is told rather than silently handed a duplicate.
